## Scope

Batch identifier: current C shared-contract catalogue reconciliation; an additive repository publication following PR69, with no new numbered batch.

Runtime behavior changed: no. The existing public-source package is restamped to the replayed catalogue version.

The settled operator scope is the current compressed C era on GitHub, coherent SAO publication groups for accumulated work, and one separate Mousecat PR. Historical C118-C120 labels identify provenance rather than current work units. This PR supplies the additive C-era catalogue reconciliation.

Publish the current 35 shared contracts and their 300 contribution links across the preserved 120-record C source generation. Keep the compression event and mapping captured on 2026-10-03 exact, retain original published commits/PR identities, and make the public catalogue agree with the already applied local transformation.

The current mapping adds a strict publication-availability binding for the two C34 recovery owners absent from public main. Their compression-time local commit/blob hashes and source record are preserved as engineering provenance. The owners remain local-unpublished and their code is absent from this PR. Source C118/C119 stay published; source C120 retains its local-unmerged verification, rendered-acceptance and redistribution limits. D1 remains OPEN, without additional C or D version credit.

## Verification

- [x] Relevant checks pass; reused evidence and its applicability are recorded.
- [x] The catalogue instrument is wired into `tools/check.sh`.
- [x] Malformed/resealed publication ledgers and three literal restored source guards reject the motivating defects.
- [x] The existing compression event and current catalogue records remain indexed in `BATCH_LOG.md`; the linked publication reconciliation record explains this unnumbered transition.
- [x] No new engine behavior is asserted.

## Validation scope and evidence

Changed inputs are catalogue/provenance/version metadata, root-document currency, and the catalogue reader/availability validator. The final Git-tree export passes 52 catalogue checks and version replay; sealed source records and frozen transition hashes remain exact across checkout line-ending settings. Three isolated restored source guards fail for the exact wrong-hash, wrong-Git-object and wrong-contract assertions. Version stamp, shipped-JAR coverage, map references, document currency, receipts, session state and gate reach also pass.

Both candidate JARs were rebuilt inside an isolated public-main worktree from the unchanged 44 public Java sources and two resources. Their entry inventory matches the public JAR exactly: 96 classes, with only `SAOVersion.class` and the inlined version constant in `SAOBridge.class` changed. All other entry bytes match. No active development source, private recovery implementation or dirty development JAR was copied.

The existing source controls retain their unchanged guarded contracts. The public-source package comparison supplies applicable runtime evidence for this metadata change. Local failed portability/session-tip checks were preserved, corrected and rerun against final inputs. Captured JSON/source-generation bytes have explicit Git attributes so their content seals survive publication. The preparation commit uses command-scoped `--no-verify` under the recorded proportionate-validation rule, avoiding a repeat of unaffected native borders. This is scoped evidence reuse, not a local full-gate claim. Protected remote `ci-verify` and `codeql-python` remain required before merge.

## What was measured before it was designed

PR137's first remote `ci-verify` failed on a false operator-attribution match in the frozen verification inventory: line1846 names `tools/operator_speech_test.py` followed by a SHA. The follow-up requires a standalone word boundary for the prose attribution detector, preserving the audit bytes. Nine inline controls and the complete tracked-text sweep pass; restoring the old regex fails both the motivating filename/hash control and the actual archived row. Genuine prose/parenthesized/verbatim attribution remains rejected. The remote failure log and literal reproduction are retained; no archive-wide exemption or local full-suite repeat was introduced. Required remote checks must pass on the follow-up head before merge.

The preserved generation already contained 120 source records. The compression audit established 35 shared contracts and 300 scoped contribution links. Public main contains the source generation through C119 but none of the current 35 contract records; exactly two C34 owner paths are absent there. The publication availability ledger is limited to those authenticated missing owners. Arbitrary missing paths remain failures.

## Operator boundary

The next protected CI run exposed two stale non-Lua registry entries and two gate-count claims. The receipts/version readers now validate Lua owner availability through the catalogue, so their `NOT_ABOUT_LUA` declarations were removed. The actual production vacuity logic passes for these two scoped subjects; restoring both old entries reproduces both remote faults. The count instrument confirms the public tree's 239 gated test files, 16 other entry points and 255 scripts, and passes its three existing mutation controls. Eight affected metadata/entrypoint consumers pass together. The current timeless publication boundary, frozen captures, runtime and package are preserved. This is scoped repair evidence; new-head remote checks remain required.

This publication reconciles the C-era metadata and package stamp. It does not promote local source delivery, rendered acceptance, redistribution permission, notebook learning or D1/D2 gameplay outcomes. Those claims retain their own evidence and authorization boundaries. The original raw local archive remains local; this PR preserves its record/hash provenance through an additive change on public main.
title: [REPO] Reconcile C shared contracts with public source
